question: UniView shell decision (triage dec-67e7d1c9 said TYPE 1). Build a universal offline file viewer for Windows, macOS, Android, iOS with one shared React+TypeScript viewer core. Options: (A) Electron (Win/macOS) + Capacitor (Android/iOS) now; installed toolchain covers it (Node 24, JDK 17, Android SDK); no Rust. (B) Tauri v2 on all four; requires installing Rust + MSVC Build Tools first; smaller binaries and faster cold start. (C) Electron+Capacitor now behind a strict FileSource/ShellBridge interface, with a scheduled Tauri prototype measured against the same 500-file benchmark before any store release or code signing, which is the point where switching becomes expensive. Constraints: development host is Windows 11 (no macOS, so iOS/macOS builds need CI later); goal is a complete working V1 soon; offline only; measurable wins on time-to-first-view, format coverage and simplicity. Evidence: docs/research (brainstorm synthesis, Vudit Desktop and Gander REA reports; Gander proves the WebView + same-origin fetch + strict CSP pattern on Android). Recommend one option with the strongest dissent.
